tags.name: Casting
tags.description: Cast to Chromecasts (Cast v2, Default Media Receiver) and AirPlay devices (audio to HomePods and speakers, video to Apple TVs). The server controls the devices itself, so every client casts the same way; devices fetch media through short-lived capability URLs. Off until an administrator sets `cast.enabled`.

get.description:
Chromecasts and AirPlay devices found with mDNS (`_googlecast._tcp`, `_airplay._tcp`, `_raop._tcp`; the AirPlay and RAOP services of one Apple device are one device) plus the admin-configured `cast.manual_devices`. Empty while casting is disabled.

**Scope:** `cast`

post.description:
Sends mDNS queries now and checks the manual devices, for at most 3 seconds, then answers like `GET /cast/devices`. One search runs at a time and at most every 5 seconds server-wide; calls in between answer with its results. No body.

**Scope:** `cast`

AirPlay PIN pairing (Apple TV), step 1: the TV shows a 4-digit PIN. One pairing per user at a time (starting again replaces the previous attempt), 8 server-wide. No body.

**Scope:** `cast`

422.description: `pairing_unsupported`: the device does not pair with a PIN (Chromecasts never need pairing).

error.message: This device needs a kind of pairing or password this server cannot do

502.description: `device_unavailable`: the device cannot be reached or did not answer.

post.description:
Step 2: the PIN shown on the TV. The credentials are kept server-wide for the device, sealed with the server key. A pairing is used once: after a wrong PIN (422, `details.fields.pin`) start again.

**Scope:** `cast`

404.description: Unknown device, or the pairing does not exist, expired or belongs to someone else.

502.description: `device_unavailable`: the device cannot be reached or did not answer.

delete.description:
Deletes the stored pairing credentials of a device (it does not have to be online).

**Scope:** `admin`

post.description:
Connects to the device (this can take a few seconds) and starts playing the queue. Every item needs its read scope and must be readable by the caller (404 otherwise); a channel plays its current program from the live offset (on-demand channels from the caller's position) and follows the schedule. A device that already has a session is taken over: that session stops with `error.code` `replaced`. At most 3 sessions per user. The device fetches media through ticket URLs on `cast.media_base_url`, else the cast listener (`cast.media_port`), else `general.public_url` — with none usable the answer is 503 `cast_unavailable`.

**Scope:** `cast`

404.description: Unknown device, or an item that does not exist or is not readable (`details.index`).

error.message: You can cast to at most 3 devices at once; stop one first

422.description: `unsupported_media` (video to an audio-only device), `pairing_required` (pair the device first), `pairing_unsupported` (the device wants a password, Home membership or verification this server cannot do), or `validation_failed` (`details.fields`).

error.message: This device cannot play video (it is a speaker)

502.description: `device_unavailable`: the device cannot be reached or did not answer.

503.description: `cast_unavailable`: no media URL the device could reach (set `cast.media_base_url`, `cast.media_port` or `general.public_url`).

error.message: Cast devices cannot reach this server

get.description:
The owner's session (ended sessions stay readable for 2 minutes). With `wait_version` the answer waits until `version` differs from it — a change of state, item, queue, volume, repeat/shuffle or a position jump — or until `timeout`. Clients poll in a loop with the last version and interpolate the position while `playing`.

**Scope:** `cast`

parameters.name: wait_version
parameters.description: Wait while the session's version equals this.

parameters.name: timeout
parameters.description: Seconds to wait at most (1–30, default 20).

delete.description:
Stops playback, disconnects from the device and records progress; answers once the device was told to stop. The owner, or an administrator for any session (its owner then sees `error.code` `admin_stopped`).

**Scope:** `cast`

post.description:
Transport (`play`, `pause`, `toggle`, `stop`, `seek`), queue navigation (`next`, `previous`, `jump` — respecting `repeat` and `shuffle`), the device volume (`volume`, `mute`) and the `repeat`/`shuffle` modes. Seeking a live channel and `next` past the end with repeat off are 409.

**Scope:** `cast`

409.description: The session ended, a live channel cannot seek, there is no next item, or nothing is playing.

502.description: `device_unavailable`: the device cannot be reached or did not answer.

504.description: `device_unavailable`: the device did not respond in time.

error.message: The device did not respond in time

put.description:
Replaces the queue and plays `items[index]` from `position_seconds`. Item rules as for `POST /cast/sessions`.

**Scope:** `cast`

post.description:
Inserts items before `position` (default: appends) without interrupting what plays; at most 1000 items in all.

**Scope:** `cast`

get.description:
What cast devices fetch. Authorised only by the session's ticket (32 random bytes, base64url) in the path — no cookies or tokens: valid for the items in the session's queue, while the session lives (+ 60 s), from the device's address (when the server sees the device's requests directly), and every request re-checks the owner's account and access. Anything else is 404. Answers `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` (no credentials) and `Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy: cross-origin` for receiver pages; `Range` reads of `stream` are exempt from the generic rate limit. Also served by the plain-HTTP cast listener (`cast.media_port`), which serves nothing else.

**Scope:** `public`

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Item ID (a media file, track or channel).

parameters.name: asset
parameters.description: `stream` (the file, `Range`), `transcode` (§6 fMP4 for video, AAC for audio; `?start=`), `art` (poster/cover JPEG, `?size=`), or `<n>.vtt` (subtitle track n as WebVTT).

parameters.name: program
parameters.description: Channel items: the file ID of the program (part of the channel's lineup).

404.description: Unknown or expired ticket, another address than the device's, an item outside the queue, or no longer readable.

AdminSettingsCast.description: Settings namespace `cast` (casting, API.md §14). Casting is off until `enabled`; devices need a media address they can reach (`media_base_url`, `media_port` or `general.public_url`).

enabled.description: Turns casting on: device discovery, cast sessions and (with `media_port`) the cast listener. Turning it off ends every session.

discovery.description: Find devices with mDNS (`_googlecast._tcp`, `_airplay._tcp`, `_raop._tcp`) on the server's networks.

manual_devices.description: Devices mDNS cannot find, e.g. on another subnet.

media_port.description: 0 turns the cast listener off; otherwise 1024–65535 (not the server's own port): a plain-HTTP listener that serves only cast ticket URLs, for devices that cannot trust the server's certificate.

media_base_url.description: Absolute http(s) URL without path, query or fragment (e.g. `https://nas.example.com`) that devices fetch media from, typically a reverse proxy with a certificate the devices trust. Empty: use `media_port`, else `general.public_url`.

AdminSettingsCastDevice.description: A cast device configured by hand.

name.description: Shown instead of the name the device reports.

CastDevice.description: A cast target: a discovered (mDNS) or admin-configured Chromecast or AirPlay device. Devices are shared by every user of the server.

id.description: Stable across restarts: the kind plus the device's own id (`chromecast-<id>`, `airplay-<MAC>`), or `manual-<host>-<port>` for manual devices.

host.description: Address (or host name of a manual device).

capabilities.description: What the device can play (speakers: audio only).

requires_pairing.description: The device needs a one-time PIN pairing (Apple TV, for AirPlay video).

paired.description: Pairing credentials are stored for this device (server-wide).

available.description: Discovered devices are listed while they answer; manual devices are unavailable after a failed connection or refresh check.

busy.description: Someone casts to this device through this server.

session_id.description: The session on this device when the caller owns it (administrators see every session id, to stop it); otherwise `null`.

enabled.description: `cast.enabled`: while casting is off, `devices` is empty.

title.description: Movie title, show title, track title, or "<number> · <channel name>".

subtitle.description: Episode code and title, year, "artist · album", or the program on air.

art_url.description: API path of the poster, cover or channel logo for the client (loaded with the client's own credentials).

code.description: `replaced` (someone started casting to the device), `idle` (30 minutes without a client request or playback), `access_revoked` (the owner's account was disabled or deleted), `cast_disabled`, `admin_stopped`, `interrupted` (stopped or taken over on the device itself), `device_unavailable`, `playback_failed`, `unsupported_media`, `pairing_required`, `pairing_unsupported`.

state.description: `idle`: the queue ended (or playback was stopped) — the session lives on; `stopped`: the session is over (readable for 2 minutes).

index.description: Index in `items` of the current item (also with shuffle on).

position_seconds.description: Position in the current item (channels: in the current program) at the time of the response; interpolate while `playing`.

duration_seconds.description: Length of the current item (channels: of the current program).

version.description: Changes with every visible change (not with the advancing position); wait for a new one with `?wait_version=`.

position_seconds.description: Where in that item to start (channels ignore it: they start at the live offset or the saved on-demand position).

action.description: `stop` stops the item but keeps the session (`DELETE` ends it); `previous` restarts an item that played longer than 3 s; `play` with nothing loaded plays the current item again.

items.description: The queue holds at most 1000 items in all.

position.description: Insert before this index (default: append). With shuffle on the new items play next; appended to a finished queue they start playing.
